Maria Chen: Quick sync 1: ACME go-live Tue. I assembled a compact customer-facing runbook for prefill/caching, batching, and streaming + the telemetry gates well use to mark renewal risk. Sharing here for comments.

Raj Patel: paste the short runbook? want 1 slide for kickoff.

Maria Chen: Runbook (consumer-facing checklist):
- PREP: pin model versions, confirm data retention TTL, collect 40 example prompts from PM.
- PREFILL: run tenant prefill for top intents (start with 40 items). TTL=24h, concurrency=6. Return prefill-results.json with attempted/succeeded/cache_hits.
- WARM: start warm pool of 5 workers, ramp over 30m to target qps with client-side jitter +-20%.
- BATCH: set batch_budget=50ms during ramp, max_batch=32. Favor frequent short batches.
- STREAM: enable streaming with chunk_size=256 and require client heartbeat every 5s. Use idempotency tokens for sessions.
- GATES: monitor p95 latency, error rate, batch_hit_rate, and negative feedback tags.

Lana Ortiz: @Maria can you paste the exact prefill call we should run post-db-migration? Kevin and I will trigger it.

Maria Chen: Prefill example to run after migration:
```
POST /v1/cache/prefill
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-prod",
  "prompts": ["what's my invoice status?","list recent orders","how to return an item"],
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "concurrency": 6
}
```

Kevin Wu: I'll run that and attach prefill-results.json when done.

onboard-bot: Reminder: kickoff call in ~24h. Agenda: prefill plan, batch policy, streaming opt-in, renewal-risk signals :bell: 

Maria Chen: Ops notes (keep latency stable):
- Use short batch_budget during ramp to avoid head-of-line latency.
- If p95 > 350ms for 5m -> reduce batch_budget or fallback to smaller model variant.
- If batch_hit_rate < 30% after 1h -> deepen prefill (top-100) and increase prefill concurrency.
- For streaming clients require idempotency tokens so replays don't create duplicate prefill entries.
- Capture first 10 queries per session for quality sampling.

Raj Patel: Post-go-live health cadence: 24h, 72h, 14d. Mark renewal risk if either: 3+ distinct failed requests in 24h OR >2 negative feedback items labeled "quality:low" within 7 days.

Lana Ortiz: I'll own the 72h health check and send a compact playbook (dashboard screenshots + exact filters).

Kevin Wu: I'll wire dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency, total tokens, batch hit rate, streaming drop rate, prefill success rate, and a composite "health_score". Posting links to dashboards and shareable filters when ready.

Maria Chen: One small ask: when you execute prefill include prefill-results.json with counts (attempted, succeeded, cache_hits) so we can compute hit_rate and tune prefill depth. :thumbsup:
